newsitem.title: USA: Health Risk Management sets rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Health Risk Management sets rights plan.

text.p: Health Risk Management Inc said Monday its board had adopted a shareholder rights plan.

"The rights plan is intended to assure fair and equal treatment for our shareholders in the event of a takeover and to encourage a potential acquiror to negotiate with the board prior to attempting a takeover," Gary McIlroy, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The plan was not adopted in response to any specific takeover threat or offer, it said.

Under the rights plan, the board declared a dividend distribution of one right for each share of common stock. Each right entitles its holder to buy one one-hundredth share of a new series of preferred stock at an exercise price of $50 per right.
The rights will become exercisable if a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of the company's common stock or announces a tender offer for 15 percent or more of its common stock.
If a person acquires 15 percent or more of the company's stock, each right would enable shareholders to acquire stock having a market value of twice the right's exercise price.
The rights distribution will be made on April 18 to shareholders of record as of the close of business that date. The rights will expire on April 4, 2007.
HRM provides health plan benefit management.
